cases.title: The Skulls In The Mail
cases.client_pitch: An oddities importer has cleaned dog, cat, and kangaroo skulls and jawbones from Australia and wants an advance customs ruling for personal display items.
cases.primary_issue: Whether cleaned taxidermied skulls and jawbones can be presented as collectors' pieces of zoological or anatomical interest.

evidence.name: Cleaned skull samples
evidence.summary: Dog, cat, and kangaroo skulls and jawbones are fully cleaned and preserved dry.

evidence.name: Cleaning process note
evidence.summary: The goods were naturally decomposed, soaked in dish soap, then treated with hydrogen peroxide.

evidence.name: Display use statement
evidence.summary: The goods will be used as personal display items.

evidence.name: Draft advance ruling
evidence.summary: The proposed classification is collectors' pieces of zoological or anatomical interest.

interactions.prompt: Ask what the goods are and why they are being imported.
Inspect the skull and jawbone samples.
Review the draft advance ruling request.

theories.label: Collectors' pieces
theories.summary: Tell the full product story: preserved animal skulls and jawbones for personal display.

theories.label: Generic animal products
theories.summary: Avoid the odd details and describe them broadly as animal products.

theories.label: Food/agriculture
theories.summary: Treat the remains as animal-origin food or agricultural goods.

full.result_text: The ruling officer accepts the product story. The skulls are treated as collectors' pieces, and the importer learns that weird facts can be useful facts.

partial.result_text: The file survives, but the client is less confident because the request made an easy display-item story sound evasive.

bad.result_text: The file closes awkwardly. Customs asks unnecessary animal-product questions because the submission ignored the actual display use.

cases.title: Retail Set Panic
cases.client_pitch: A gift-box distributor wants one tariff answer for multiple retail bundles and assumes every box sold together is a set.
cases.primary_issue: Whether goods put together for retail sale are intended to be used together before essential character is considered.

evidence.name: Canned goods assortment
evidence.summary: Shrimp, pate, cheese, bacon, and cocktail sausages are packaged together but do not form a single joint use.

evidence.name: Sandwich and fries
evidence.summary: A beef sandwich and fries form a meal; essential character is the sandwich.

evidence.name: Spaghetti meal kit
evidence.summary: Uncooked spaghetti, grated cheese, and tomato sauce form a meal kit; essential character is spaghetti.

evidence.name: Coffee, cup, and saucer
evidence.summary: A coffee jar with a ceramic cup and saucer is a retail selection, not a set for the rule.

evidence.name: Set rule note
evidence.summary: The set rule applies to goods intended to be used together; essential character comes after that threshold.

interactions.prompt: Ask whether customers use each bundle together or just receive a selection.
Sort each bundle into set or selection, then assign essential character where the rule applies.
Explain why not every retail box is a set.

theories.label: Threshold first
theories.summary: Ask whether the goods are intended to be used together before applying essential character.

theories.label: All boxes are sets
theories.summary: Treat everything packaged together for retail sale as a set.

theories.label: Highest value wins
theories.summary: Pick the most valuable component in each bundle.

full.result_text: The officer accepts the threshold analysis. The client learns that a box is not a magic spell.

partial.result_text: The advice is mostly useful, but one bundle is still exposed to a bad classification position.

bad.result_text: The client leaves with a rule that is too broad and an audit file that will age badly.

cases.title: Dog Chew Apocalypse
cases.client_pitch: A pet product importer has six dog chew SKUs under review, including a cheese-based chew customs has flagged as a compliance priority.
cases.primary_issue: Whether each chew is classified by material composition and production method rather than consumer-facing purpose.

evidence.name: Plain cut bone sample
evidence.summary: A cleaned and simply cut bone chew.

evidence.name: Bone with tissue sample
evidence.summary: A bone chew retaining meat, cartilage, ears, tendons, snouts, or other offal.

evidence.name: Extruded chew formula
evidence.summary: Animal or vegetable inputs are extruded with binders and flavourings.

evidence.name: Rawhide chew sample
evidence.summary: Flavoured rawhide sold for chewing but made from leather.

evidence.name: Braided rawhide formula
evidence.summary: Rawhide braided with starch and protein.

evidence.name: Yak cheese ingredient sheet
evidence.summary: Yak milk, lime juice, and sea salt are hardened and dried into a chew.

evidence.name: Compliance priority notice
evidence.summary: Cheese-based dog chews are a customs compliance priority.

interactions.prompt: Ask which SKUs are detained and which products contain dairy.
Inspect all detained dog chew samples.
Ask how the chews are cut, extruded, braided, hardened, and flavoured.
Classify each SKU and flag the highest-risk product.

theories.label: Composition and process
theories.summary: Classify each SKU by what it is made of and how it is produced, then isolate the cheese chew risk.

theories.label: All pet food
theories.summary: Classify everything as pet food because dogs chew it.

theories.label: All animal products
theories.summary: Classify all animal-origin chews under one animal-product bucket.

full.result_text: The importer gets a usable SKU map and isolates the cheese chew before supply-management duties become a disaster.

partial.result_text: Most SKUs are contained, but the memo still leaves avoidable ambiguity.

bad.result_text: The cheese chew risk was missed. Customs has found the expensive SKU before the lawyer did.

cases.title: Meaning Of "Of"
cases.client_pitch: A gelato powder importer faces a 250.5 percent dairy duty because customs says flavoured powders are food preparations of milk.
cases.primary_issue: Whether 'of milk' means merely containing milk or being based on milk through functional essentiality.

evidence.name: Ingredient percentage sheet
evidence.summary: Sugar is the largest component by percentage and milk is less than 50 percent.

evidence.name: Customs dairy assessment
evidence.summary: Customs applied a 250.5 percent dairy duty because the powders contain milk.

evidence.name: Of means based on note
evidence.summary: Prior reasoning says 'of' means 'based on,' but the meaning of based on needs work.

evidence.name: Expert functional contribution
evidence.summary: Each ingredient contributes to taste, texture, quality, and performance; milk is not more essential than the others.

evidence.name: Rehydration process note
evidence.summary: The powders require milk or other inputs during manufacturing; the finished performance depends on multiple ingredients.

evidence.name: Duty exposure summary
evidence.summary: The case turns a duty-free position into a 250.5 percent exposure if customs wins.

interactions.prompt: Ask what customs assessed and why the client thinks it is wrong.
Review the powder composition and prior wording notes.
Ask what each ingredient does in the finished gelato or pastry product.

theories.label: Based on essentiality
theories.summary: 'Of milk' means based on milk; milk must be more essential to purpose and function than the other ingredients.

theories.label: Less than half milk
theories.summary: Milk is under 50 percent, so the powders cannot be of milk.

theories.label: Ice cream means dairy
theories.summary: The powders make ice cream, so customs is probably right.

argument_moves.label: Concede milk is important, not controlling

full.result_text: The panel accepts that containing milk is not enough. The powders are not based on milk because milk is not more essential than the other functional ingredients.

partial.result_text: The percentage point helps, but the argument lacks the expert foundation needed for a clean win.

bad.result_text: Customs keeps the dairy theory. The client pays for the missing expert record.

precedent_notes.title: Advance rulings need a product story
precedent_notes.effect: Unlocks stronger advance-ruling dialogue options in later cases.

precedent_notes.title: Essential character only matters after the set rule applies
precedent_notes.effect: Unlocks threshold-first sorting prompts in bundled-good cases.

precedent_notes.title: Production method beats product vibes
precedent_notes.effect: Unlocks production-process questions in manufactured-good cases.

precedent_notes.title: Of means based on; based on means essentiality
precedent_notes.effect: Unlocks functional-essentiality argument moves in ingredient cases.
